records.mutation: name the false-contradiction trap that replaces the unfollowed "do not assume one reading" clause
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored 0 and every one failed the same way: the student fixed the product reading, derived that an agent would then know the partner value, declared the problem logically inconsistent, and closed by asserting an unverified candidate (six of eight converged on the same wrong divisor, and two also truncated at the token cap while still relitigating the reading). The incumbent's abstract prohibition ('do not case-split externally, assume one reading, and restart') was visibly ignored, so I replaced only that clause with an operational statement of what the apparent contradiction actually proves, keeping the surviving filtering and verification wording intact and adding just four net tokens.

records.mutation: delete unused k=1-gives-a-line parenthetical (shorter, removes k-symbol collision)
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts were correct and every one used the modulus-ratio first move, the nth-root check on the constant, the x+iy/complete-the-square step, and an explicit-root numeric check against the original equation; not one rollout ever invoked the degenerate line case. Worse, all 8 independently reused k as the root INDEX (k=0..5), so the parenthetical claim about k=1 collides with their own notation and risks planting a false belief. Deleting only that clause leaves every load-bearing instruction intact while making the hint 7 tokens shorter.

records.mutation: ban symbolic tan-angle formula, pay for it by trimming far-edge justification
records.subagent_summary: All 5 of 8 failures were token-cap truncations with no value stated, and the dominant signature was the student abandoning the hint's numeric shoelace instruction to build a symbolic tilt-angle formula, then burning thousands of tokens on contradiction loops between that formula and its own numeric checks (heavy tan/theta and repeated self-correction markers; the 3 successes had far fewer). The edit names that exact trap ('pick two specific tilt angles and never build a symbolic tan-angle formula') and pays for the words by deleting the far-edge justification clause, which is inert reasoning no rollout used, leaving the hint slightly shorter than the incumbent.

records.mutation: name the exact root-cap degree (n, not n-1 or n+1)
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 5/8 with no truncation (all finish_reason stop); every failure was the same single misstep, mis-sizing the per-polynomial root cap by taking the finite-difference degree n-1 or the interpolation point count n+1 instead of deg(P-L)=n, then multiplying that wrong cap by the family size. All five successes used the caps value correctly. I therefore replaced the vague trap clause about differencing with an explicit statement that subtracting an affine function preserves the leading term so the cap is exactly n, and named both off-by-one distractors; the rest of the proven text is unchanged.

records.mutation: add back-substitution sanity check on fitted constants
records.subagent_summary: Both failing rollouts of 8 fit the curve constants correctly, then wrote the curve with numerator and denominator swapped, hit a self-contradiction, and spent the entire 16384-token budget re-deriving without ever stating a value (finish_reason=length); the six correct rollouts differed only in getting that substitution right. The edit adds one concrete check (re-evaluate a given point in the original expression right after fitting) and folds the anti-looping stop rule into the existing repair clause, leaving the proven reduce-to-one-unknown and shoelace text intact.

records.mutation: replace multi-part reporting rule: single graded value from the first labelled part
records.subagent_summary: All eight rollouts scored 0 with finish_reason stop (no truncation), so this is not a budget problem. Two rollouts derived the first part correctly using the state/timing framing the hint already teaches, but then presented a second part's value last, so the graded extraction picked the wrong number - the incumbent's 'one value per part' instruction actively invited that. I therefore replaced only that closing clause with an explicit single-graded-value rule, and paid for it by trimming the 'legal moves form a small state graph' phrase that no rollout visibly used, leaving the proven state-representation, LIFO-timing, path-product, and anti-uniformity clauses untouched.

records.mutation: sharpen stop-trigger and inline the unprescribed-monomial rule
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts hit the 16384-token cap with finish_reason=length and produced no stated value, so reward was 0/8 despite several rollouts reaching a correct closed form mid-trace and then discarding it to re-derive or sanity-check it again. The incumbent's standalone 'note which monomial is NOT prescribed ... never use it' sentence was visibly misparsed into confusion about vanishing at nodes, so it is folded into the product-construction step, and the vague 'commit to one value' tail is replaced by an event-triggered stop ('the moment a closed form appears ... do not re-derive it') that fires exactly where the traces stalled; net length is +5 tokens.

records.mutation: replace vague 'maximum-feasible-count interpretation' with the concrete gcd move; generalize street/house nouns to units/groups
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 and terminated cleanly (no truncation), so train accuracy cannot rise and the only lever is transfer. Multiple rollouts visibly stalled re-reading the incumbent's abstract clause about the 'intended maximum-feasible-count interpretation' before independently deriving the gcd themselves, so that clause was the weakest text; I replaced it with the concrete technique it was gesturing at and generalized the domain-specific 'street/house' wording to 'equal-group/identical units', ending one token shorter than the incumbent.

records.mutation: replace dead sign-slip clause with symbol-collision and identity-not-one-point traps
records.subagent_summary: 5 of 8 rollouts were correct and all 8 followed the affine link and fixed the shift constant from the point values, so the core of the incumbent is working; the clause warning about sign slips when re-expanding q was dead weight because every rollout already evaluated through q = -p + b. Both non-truncation failures instead died the same way: they reused the same letter for the shift constant and for a coefficient of p, then imposed the collapsed relation at a single input rather than as an identity, under-determining the coefficients and guessing. I swapped only that one unused clause for those two traps, keeping the rest of the proven wording and the length essentially unchanged.

records.mutation: replace unused duplicate-check clause with stage-vs-operation counting rule; ban special-case patching
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 0/8 with 7 of 8 truncated at the token cap after thousands of tokens of re-derivation. No rollout ever used the incumbent's 'each label exactly once / redo the stage' bookkeeping clause, so those tokens were dead weight; instead the dominant concrete misstep was conflating one stage with one full operation while tracing small sizes, which then made traces disagree with candidate formulas and triggered endless restarts. Two rollouts that did reach a stated value got there by patching a formula with an n=1 special case, so I reallocated the unused clause into an explicit stage-vs-operation counting rule plus a ban on special-case patching, and the result is shorter than the incumbent.
